# ruleId: # EVERY line below carries `review-by:<YYYY-MM-DD>`. That is not decoration:
# tests/unit/zap-rules-have-review-dates.test.ts fails a PR if a suppression has
# no date, and the NIGHTLY job fails once a date passes — so a suppression
# cannot quietly outlive its reason, without a calendar date being able to
# redden an unrelated hotfix. (The expiry check deliberately does NOT sit in the
# PR-blocking unit suite; see that test's header.)
# ## Why this list is long, and why it has to be
# `cmd_options` no longer carries `-I` ("do not return failure on warning"), so
# ANY unsuppressed WARN now fails the job. `docs/security/zap-triage-2026-07-15.md`
# already accepted NINE rule ids with documented reasoning, and the reasons below
# are quoted from it rather than re-derived. Without them the nightly job would
# be red from its first post-merge run and every run after — turning the new
# Telegram channel into exactly the alert fatigue this change set out to end.
# ## The cost of a global IGNORE
# rules.tsv has no URL scoping, so each line also hides the NOT-yet-accepted
# variant of its own class. Four are worth naming:
#   10055 also covers the "CSP directives with no default-src fallback" finding
#         that was FIXED in the 2026-07-15 PR. Suppressing the id hides a
#         regression of that fix, so `tests/unit/csp-directive-floor.test.ts`
#         pins base-uri/object-src/form-action directly on the three configs —
#         that test, not the scan, is now what guards it.
#   10202 hides any future form-post surface that genuinely lacks a token.
#   10063 is accepted for static JS/CSS chunks, but also hides Permissions-
#         Policy vanishing from the HTML routes that carry it. The same
#         csp-directive-floor.test.ts pins the header on all three configs
#         (issue 2100) — the test, not the scan, guards the HTML routes.
#   10044 is accepted for ONE known redirect (the store apex 307, whose body is
#         the public 404 markup), but also hides a future redirect that
#         serialises session or PII into its body. No deterministic gate can
#         pin a runtime redirect body at the unit tier; this is an accepted
#         residual (Ruling ZAP-10044 in docs/RULINGS.md), bounded by its
#         review-by date.
# ## Removal plan
# 10055 and 10038 come OFF this list when the CSP nonce work lands
# (docs/security/csp-hardening-plan.md). Leaving them after that would hide a
# regression rather than silence a known residual.

# ruleId: # ── Accepted in docs/security/zap-triage-2026-07-15.md, reasons quoted ──────

comment: User-controllable HTML attribute - PLAUSIBLE-only; React escapes attribute interpolation and every API edge is Zod-validated; review-by:2027-03-31
Dangerous JS functions - eval inside a bundled third-party SDK, the same dependency behind the CSP unsafe-eval debt; review-by:2026-12-31
SRI missing - marketing-pixel/OneSignal SDK loaders that self-update; pinning hashes breaks them on every vendor release. Bounded by the fixed script-src allowlist; review-by:2027-03-31
COEP missing - require-corp breaks cross-origin images/pixels storefront-wide; no SharedArrayBuffer use so no benefit; review-by:2027-03-31
Sec-Fetch-Dest missing - request-side header set by browsers not servers; ZAP noise on non-browser requests; review-by:2027-03-31
Re-examine Cache-Control - advisory on intentionally-cached public pages; caching policy is deliberate; review-by:2027-03-31
Non-storable content - advisory; responses marked non-cacheable are auth-adjacent, which is correct; review-by:2027-03-31
Base64 disclosure - Next.js inline RSC/flight payloads, not secrets; gitleaks + client-secret-scan gate real leakage; review-by:2027-03-31
Session-management response identified - informational fingerprint of the auth flow, not a defect; review-by:2027-03-31
CSP unsafe-inline/unsafe-eval - Next.js App Router requirement, needs nonce work. ALSO masks the default-src-fallback fix; csp-directive-floor.test.ts guards that; review-by:2026-12-31

CSP header not set - fires on the apex 307 redirect; every 200 carries a CSP (verified against production 2026-09-11). This IGNORE is global (no URL scoping), so a config that dropped the header from a real 200 would go undetected here — tests/unit/csp-directive-floor.test.ts now asserts every config declares Content-Security-Policy at all, closing that gap deterministically at the PR-blocking tier; review-by:2026-12-31
Anti-CSRF tokens - double-submit cookie + X-CSRF-Token header, not a hidden form field; review-by:2027-03-31
